fixes.explanation: Perfect, baker. Paul says, "For now we can go on living, as long as you are standing firm in the Lord." (1 Thessalonians 3:8). Timothy had just come back with good news about their faith, and Paul says that reassured them (1 Thessalonians 3:6-7). Standing firm is how much he cares about them.

Close, friend, but Paul doesn't name Demetrius here. He says, "…I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us." (1 Thessalonians 2:18). Satan is the one he names. Don't feel bad, I once blamed the mustache for a burnt batch, and it was totally innocent that time.

Nice guess, friend, but Paul doesn't name Alexander here. He writes, "…I, Paul, tried again and again—but Satan obstructed us." (1 Thessalonians 2:18). Again and AGAIN he tries, like someone hitting redial on a busy line. Satan is the one he says stood in the way.

Good thinking, friend, but Galatia isn't who Paul points to here. He says, "…who is our hope, our joy, our crown of boasting, if it is not you yourselves…" (1 Thessalonians 2:19). He's talking straight to the Thessalonians. Then he adds, "You are indeed our glory and our joy." (1 Thessalonians 2:20). That's a man bragging on his people like a proud dad.

Not this time, friend. Paul does mention the churches in Judea earlier in the letter (1 Thessalonians 2:14), but here he says, "…if it is not you yourselves…" (1 Thessalonians 2:19). He's talking directly to the Thessalonians. He finishes with "You are indeed our glory and our joy." (1 Thessalonians 2:20).

Not quite, friend. Paul says, "…when we were with you, we kept warning you that we would suffer persecution; and as you know, it has come to pass." (1 Thessalonians 3:4). He warned them about suffering. Nobody promised them a free pass.

Good guess, friend, but Paul doesn't mention that here. He says they pray to see the Thessalonians face to face "…and supply what is lacking in your faith." (1 Thessalonians 3:10). Their goal is to help the Thessalonians' faith, not collect anything.

Yes, baker, you read it right. Paul writes, "…may the Lord cause you to increase and overflow with love for one another and for everyone else, just as our love for you overflows…" (1 Thessalonians 3:12). "…for one another and for everyone else…" Overflowing means it doesn't stop at the edge of the cup.
